statement: For a multi-stage dynamic optimization problem exhibiting optimal substructure, the optimal cost-to-go (or value function) and optimal policy are determined recursively by backward induction using the Bellman recurrence relation $J_k^*(\mathbf{x}_{n-k}) = \min_{\mathbf{u}_{n-k}} \left\{ \hat{f}(\mathbf{x}_{n-k}, \mathbf{u}_{n-k}) + J_{k-1}^*\left(\hat{\mathbf{g}}(\mathbf{x}_{n-k}, \mathbf{u}_{n-k})\right) \right\}$, starting from the terminal boundary condition and stepping backward stage by stage to obtain the optimal solution value $V_1$ at the initial state and recover the optimal decision variables.

steps.text: By optimal substructure, simplify the multi-stage decision problem by decomposing it into simpler sub-problems recursively over time, defining a sequence of value functions (or cost-to-go functions) $V_t$ or $J_k^*$ representing the value of the state at each stage, anchored by the terminal condition $J(t_1) = b(\mathbf{x}(t_1), t_1)$ (or $V_{T+1} = 0$).

Express the optimal cost-to-go at stage $k$ via the discrete recurrence relation analog to the continuous Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation (the Bellman equation): $J_k^*(\mathbf{x}_{n-k}) = \min_{\mathbf{u}_{n-k}} \left\{ \hat{f}(\mathbf{x}_{n-k}, \mathbf{u}_{n-k}) + J_{k-1}^*\left(\hat{\mathbf{g}}(\mathbf{x}_{n-k}, \mathbf{u}_{n-k})\right) \right\}$, which relates the current decision and stage cost to the subsequent optimal cost-to-go.

Compute the value functions by backward recursion: initializing from the terminal condition, use the recurrence at each step so that once $V_i$ (or $J_{k-1}^*$) has been calculated for the needed states, the operation yields $V_{i-1}$ (or $J_k^*$) for those states, proceeding backwards until $V_1$ (or $J_n^*$) at the initial state of the system is obtained as the value of the optimal solution.
Recover the optimal values of the decision variables $\mathbf{u}^*$ one by one by tracking back through the calculations already performed from the initial state.

assumptions.assumption: The decision problem exhibits optimal substructure.
assumptions.breaks_when: An optimal solution to the overall problem cannot be constructed from optimal solutions to its sub-problems.

assumptions.assumption: The problem can be decomposed into a discrete sequence of stages with well-defined transitions and boundary conditions.
assumptions.breaks_when: Decisions cannot be separated sequentially over time or the terminal boundary condition is undefined.
Sub-problems do not overlap (e.g., standard divide-and-conquer where sub-problems are completely independent and disjoint), making table reuse inapplicable.

failure_modes.signature: Sub-problem optimization does not lead to a globally optimal solution.
failure_modes.cause: Decisions spanning multiple points in time do not break apart recursively or stage costs depend non-separably on past decision trajectories.

failure_modes.mode: Curse of dimensionality in continuous state approximation
failure_modes.signature: Discrete approximation requires intractable computation or memory.
failure_modes.cause: Discretizing continuous state space $\mathbf{x}$ and control space $\mathbf{u}$ over $n$ intervals leads to exponential growth in the number of states needed to evaluate $J_k^*$.
